newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares rise, seen up amid sideways trend.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares rise, seen up amid sideways trend.

text.p: Polish shares rose for the third consecutive session and analysts expected further growth this week with investors hunting for bargains, but said the market's upside was limited.
The main market's WIG index rose 1.5 percent, to 16,179.7, and trade rose 8.2 percent to 134.6 million zlotys ($42.1 million) on all three markets as 74 issues rose, 21 fell and nine were flat.
"There is a chance for the market to rise at least a little, especially if you take into account recent falls of certain stocks," said Czeslaw Pospieszynski of PBI brokerage.

Analysts said the bourse was likely to keep swinging in its longer-term horizontal trend as forthcoming elections due in September and busy primary market were cooling investor mood while current prices did not justify significant falls.

They said the bourse's current valuation at 15.7 times historic earnings was fair, but said there were some undervalued stocks which might be pushing the bourse up. Analysts said Bank Handlowy, which is offering one- billion-zloty ($312 million) worth of shares on the primary market, household appliances maker Amica Wronki which is offering shares worth more than 100 million zlotys ($31.3 million) and expected June sale of copper giant KGHM were drawing capital from the bourse.
But they said in the longer-term listing of the large firms could attract additional capital to the bourse, increasing its capitalisation and liquidity.
Analysts could not explain carpet maket Novita nine-percent jump but said the stock was likely to fall on Tuesday, following Monday's strong selling after price fixing.

Analysts said paintmakers Polifarb Cieszyn and Polifarb Wroclaw which rose 2.2 and 5.8 percent respectively, moved on Friday's news they have removed obstacles to their merger, but said they were unlikely to extend their gains. REUTERS
